content: POST /api/admin/bookings/:id/promote AdminController -> BookingService::promoteFromWaitlist(bookingId): 1. UPDATE bookings SET is_waiting_list=0 WHERE id=? (booking_status stays 'pending', payment_status stays 'pending') 2. NotificationService::sendWaitlistPromotionNotification(bookingId) -> Email customer: "A spot has opened up — pay within 48 hours" Customer pays: POST /api/bookings/:id/pay BookingController -> PaymentService (credit first, then Stripe if needed) -> booking confirmed Lazy expiry (runs on each booking list read): BookingService::expireUnpaidPromotions() -> Finds promoted bookings (is_waiting_list=0, payment_status=pending, session has passed or >48h since promotion) -> Cancels them, frees the spot

title: Notification events
snippet: All outbound notifications flow through `NotificationService`. The table below lists every event, which channels fire, and what triggers the dispatch.
content: All outbound notifications flow through `NotificationService`. The table below lists every event, which channels fire, and what triggers the dispatch. | Event | Channels | Trigger | |---|---|---| | Email verification | Email | Registration, or resend request | | Password reset | Email | Forgotten password request | | Email change verification | Email | Customer updates their email address | | Booking confirmation | Email | Payment confirmed (Stripe or credit) | | Booking cancellation | Email | Customer cancels a booking | | Session cancellation | Email | Admin cancels a session (fires per affected booking) | | Session reminder | Email | Cron — 24 h before session start (see Scheduled Tasks) | | Attendance confirmation request | Email | Cron — configurable hours before session (default 24 h, see Notification Templates) | | Payment request | Email | Instructor marks booking attended and payment_status is pending | | Payment reminder | Email | Post-session sweep — attended but unpaid | | Group broadcast | Email | Admin sends message to a group | | Staff subscriber alert | Email, In-app | New booking / cancellation / attendance reminder, if staff has a subscription for that activity | | Test email | Email | Admin → Settings → Notification Services | Staff subscribers receive notifications through `dispatchToSubscribers()` for `new_booking`, `cancellation`, and `attendance_reminder` events. Admins with `in_app_notifications = 1` always receive in-app alerts for those events even without a subscription.

title: Notification channels
snippet: Email is the only customer notification channel (SMS/WhatsApp via Bird were removed in October 2026). Staff also get in-app toasts. **The email toggle
content: Email is the only customer notification channel (SMS/WhatsApp via Bird were removed in October 2026). Staff also get in-app toasts. **The email toggle is honoured.** `NotificationService::dispatch()` skips email when the user's `user_preferences.email_notifications = 0` (no row or NULL = on, via `UserRepository::emailPrefAllows()`). Staff subscriber emails check the same preference. Use it to silence notification emails for an account, e.g. auto-booked sessions before go-live. **Booking does not require email to be on.** A customer with email off can still book; they just aren't emailed. **Toggle switches post a hidden input that is always present** (`value="0"` or `"1"`). Read them with `postFlag('field')` from `app/Helpers/helpers.php`, never `isset($_POST['field'])`. **App-wide kill switch:** `app_settings.notifications_disabled = '1'` stops customer emails and staff subscriber emails/in-app alerts. Admin and instructor broadcasts go through the same gate (`NotificationService::sendToUser()`) and refuse with 409 while it's on. **Staff subscription events** are listed once in `NotificationSubscriptionRepository::EVENT_LABELS` (must match the `event_type` enum; `SubscriptionEventTypesTest` enforces it). `eventTypesForRole()` drives the form and route validation. Send an event with `NotificationService::notifySubscribers($eventType, $subject, $summary, $activityId, $sessionId)`; unknown types throw. Fan-out only reaches staff (admin, super_admin, instructor). | Event | Sent from | |---|---| | `new_session_booking` / `new_room_booking` | `sendBookingConfirmation()` (room hire → `new_room_booking`) | | `cancellation` | `sendCancellationNotification()` | | `attendance_reminder` | `sendSessionReminder()` | | `payment_received` | `PaymentService` — Stripe single/batch and account credit | | `payment_failed` | `StripeWebhookService` via `POST /api/payments/stripe/webhook` (signature-verified, needs `stripe_webhook_secret`) | | `withdrawal_requested` | `BookingController::requestWithdrawal()` | | `new_user` | `AuthService::register()` | **Customer session reminders:** a customer's own reminder is sent only for activities in their "Booking reminders" choices (`attendance_reminder` rows; `activity_id` NULL = all). New customers get an "All" row (`addDefaultCustomerReminder()`); existing ones were backfilled by `2026_10_14_customer_reminder_default.sql`. Customer rows are never fanned out to other users.

snippet: Emails are sent by either `SmtpService` or `ResendService`, selected by the `mail_driver` setting (default: `resend`). `NotificationService` reads the
content: Emails are sent by either `SmtpService` or `ResendService`, selected by the `mail_driver` setting (default: `resend`). `NotificationService` reads the driver at construction time and routes all `sendEmail()` calls to the active mailer. 1. Fetch booking details (user email, activity, session date) 2. Render HTML template 3. $this->mailer->send(to, subject, html): SmtpService path: a. Read smtp_host, smtp_port, smtp_username, smtp_password, smtp_encryption from app_settings b. If smtp_host is empty -> log to logs/emails.log (fallback) c. Connect via stream_socket_client(), STARTTLS (port 587) or SSL (port 465) d. AUTH LOGIN, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, QUIT ResendService path: a. Read resend_api_key from app_settings (AES-256-GCM encrypted) b. If no API key -> log to logs/emails.log (local dev fallback) c. POST to https://api.resend.com/emails via cURL Settings priority: `app_settings` DB table → env var fallback → hardcoded default. **To test emails locally (SMTP):** Run Mailpit (`brew install mailpit`, then `mailpit`). Configure in Settings: driver=SMTP, host=`localhost`, port=`1025`, encryption=`none`. Captured mail appears at `http://localhost:8025`. **To test emails locally (Resend):** Leave `resend_api_key` unset in `app_settings`. Emails print to `logs/emails.log` instead.

title: Attendance confirmation flow (soft-decline)
snippet: The attendance confirmation is a yes/no email sent to the account holder before the session. "No" is a **soft decline** — it records the response but
content: The attendance confirmation is a yes/no email sent to the account holder before the session. "No" is a **soft decline** — it records the response but does not cancel or refund. ↓ Clicks YES → POST /booking/confirm-attendance?token=…&response=yes AttendanceConfirmationService::processResponse() - booking_status → 'confirmed', attendance_response = 'yes' - No further action (payment handled separately via AttendanceService) Clicks NO → POST /booking/confirm-attendance?token=…&response=no AttendanceConfirmationService::processResponse() - attendance_response = 'no' - booking_status stays as-is (NOT cancelled, NOT refunded) - Returns: "Got it — you have been marked as not attending." Downstream when instructor marks attendance (`AttendanceService::markAttendance()`): → NotificationService::sendPaymentRequest() — asks customer to pay status = 'absent' + payment_status = 'paid' + booking_status != 'pending' → BookingService::cancelBooking(..., isAdmin: true) with reason 'Absent — refund issued' (same refund as a cancellation: net of discount, capped for block sessions, to account credit) status = 'absent' + booking_status = 'pending' → BookingRepository::cancelWithReason('Absent and booking not confirmed') (nothing was paid, so no refund) The instructor session-detail view shows an **Unpaid** badge for any booking with `payment_status = 'pending'` (visible to both instructors and admins — not admin-only).

title: Notification templates
snippet: Admins (super_admin only) can override the subject, body, and short summary for 7 notification types without a code deploy. The system checks for a DB
content:
Admins (super_admin only) can override the subject, body, and short summary for 7 notification types without a code deploy. The system checks for a DB override first and falls back to the hardcoded default if none exists. **DB table:** `notification_templates` | Column | Type | Notes | |---|---|---| | `notification_type` | varchar(50) UNIQUE | One of the 7 editable types | | `email_subject` | varchar(255) NULL | NULL = use hardcoded default | | `email_body` | text NULL | Plain text; newlines → `
` on send | | `short_message` | varchar(500) NULL | Plain-text summary for in-app notifications and staff alert emails | | `send_day_of_week` | tinyint NULL | Session reminder + attendance confirmation only; 1=Mon…7=Sun (ISO-8601), NULL=Monday | **Editable types:** `booking_confirmation`, `cancellation_notification`, `session_cancellation`, `session_reminder`, `attendance_confirmation`, `payment_request`, `payment_reminder`. **Resolution:** `NotificationService::resolveTemplate(type, ...)` queries `NotificationTemplateRepository::getByType()`. Non-null DB fields override their hardcoded counterparts; null fields fall through to the hardcoded string. **Placeholders:** `{participant_name}`, `{activity_title}`, `{date}`, `{time}`, `{amount}`, `{venue}`, `{refund_amount}`, `{first_name}`, `{booking_id}`, `{yes_url}`, `{no_url}` — availability varies by type. Required placeholders are validated client-side and server-side on save. **`send_day_of_week`:** Controls which day of the week reminders are batched and sent. Both cron scripts (`send-session-reminders.php`, `send-attendance-confirmations.php`) run daily, check if today matches the configured day (default Monday), then send reminders for all sessions from the following day through the next 7 days. Sessions already reminded (`reminder_sent_at IS NOT NULL`) are skipped automatically. **Admin UI:** `GET /admin/notification-templates/{type}` (super_admin only). Left nav lists all 7 types with a dot indicator for customised ones. Right form: placeholder toolbar, email subject input, email body textarea, short summary textarea, and day-of-week dropdown for time-based types. Inputs pre-fill with the hardcoded defaults when no DB override exists. "Reset to default" button clears all fields for the current type. **Key files:** `NotificationTemplateRepository.php`, `NotificationService::resolveTemplate()`, `app/Views/admin/notification-templates.php`, `app/Routes/admin.php` (~line 2881), `scripts/send-session-reminders.php`, `scripts/send-attendance-confirmations.php`. ---

title: No innerHTML — ever
snippet: This is a hard security rule. Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with any dynamic data. Build DOM trees with DOM methods: fun
content: This is a hard security rule. Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with any dynamic data. Build DOM trees with DOM methods: function renderBookingRow(booking) { const tr = document.createElement('tr'); const td = document.createElement('td'); td.textContent = booking.activity_title;   // safe — escapes all HTML tr.appendChild(td); const statusTd = document.createElement('td'); statusTd.textContent = booking.status; tr.appendChild(statusTd); return tr; } // To clear and repopulate a table body: tbody.replaceChildren(...bookings.map(renderBookingRow)); // To remove a node: row.remove(); The reason: any user-controlled string injected via `innerHTML` becomes executable HTML. Even if you think the value is safe, it is not safe — XSS vulnerabilities are subtle and context-dependent.

title: CSRF protection
snippet: Every state-changing request requires a valid CSRF token. The CSRF token is a 64-character hex string stored in a `csrf_token` cookie (SameSite=Strict
content: Every state-changing request requires a valid CSRF token. The CSRF token is a 64-character hex string stored in a `csrf_token` cookie (SameSite=Strict, NOT HttpOnly — JavaScript must read it). **HTML forms:** Include a hidden field. **JavaScript API calls:** Append the token to the URL. const token = document.cookie.match(/csrf_token=([^;]+)/)?.[1] ?? ''; return path + (path.includes('?') ? '&' : '?') + '_csrf_token=' + encodeURIComponent(token); } Server validation (`validateCsrfToken()` in `auth.php`): checks `X-CSRF-Token` header, then `$_POST['_csrf_token']`, then `$_GET['_csrf_token']`. Uses `hash_equals()` for timing-safe comparison. API routes call `$this->verifyCsrf()` inside `requireAuth()` automatically. HTML form POSTs are validated in `index.php` before reaching any route handler. **Session expiry recovery:** The CSRF token is stored as a session cookie (expires when the browser closes). If a user loads the login/register page, closes and reopens the browser, then submits the form, the cookie is gone and validation fails. Rather than showing a dead-end error page, `index.php` redirects back to the same URL with `?csrf_retry=1`, which triggers a fresh GET that re-issues the cookie. The page then shows "Your session expired. Please try again." and the next submit succeeds.

title: JWT tokens
snippet: - Algorithm: HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) - Secret: `JWT_SECRET` environment variable - Payload: `{ user_id, email, role, iat, exp }` - Expiry: 120 minutes; ro
content: - Algorithm: HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) - Secret: `JWT_SECRET` environment variable - Payload: `{ user_id, email, role, iat, exp }` - Expiry: 120 minutes; rolling refresh on each page navigation creates a 120-minute inactivity window - Stored in `auth_token` cookie: HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure when HTTPS **Password invalidation:** if `users.password_changed_at > JWT.iat`, the token is rejected even if not expired. This immediately invalidates all existing sessions when a user changes their password.

content: Repositories that perform dynamic UPDATE queries maintain an explicit whitelist of allowed column names: private array $allowedUpdateColumns = [ 'first_name', 'last_name', 'phone', 'date_of_birth', 'account_type' ]; public function updateUser(int $id, array $data): bool { $sets = []; $params = []; foreach ($data as $col => $val) { if (!in_array($col, $this->allowedUpdateColumns)) { continue;  // silently skip — never trust input column names } $sets[] = "$col = ?"; $params[] = $val; } // ... } This prevents an attacker from passing `role=super_admin` in a JSON body and having it inserted into a dynamic UPDATE statement. ---

content: The `mcp/` directory contains a set of MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that let AI assistants — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, or any MCP-compatible client — interact with the booking system through natural language.

title: What the MCP layer is and why it exists
snippet: The MCP server is a read/write interface to the booking system's existing REST API. It requires no PHP changes and adds no new server-side code. An ad
content: The MCP server is a read/write interface to the booking system's existing REST API. It requires no PHP changes and adds no new server-side code. An admin can ask Claude "Pull today's bookings" or "Give me a revenue summary for this month" and receive an accurate, structured answer. It authenticates against the PHP API using the same JWT flow as the web app.

title: Directory structure
snippet: ├── packages/ │ ├── core/ # Shared API client + all customer-tier tools │ ├── customer/ # Customer MCP server (stdio) │ ├── instructor/ # Instructor M
content: ├── packages/ │   ├── core/       # Shared API client + all customer-tier tools │   ├── customer/   # Customer MCP server (stdio) │   ├── instructor/ # Instructor MCP server (stdio) │   └── admin/      # Admin MCP server (stdio) — all tools + 4 prompts └── workers/        # Cloudflare Worker (HTTP transport, all three roles) The packages follow a tiered model: `core` provides the base customer tools, `instructor` adds session and attendance tools on top, and `admin` adds the full set of resource management, reporting, and admin booking tools. Destructive or financial actions require `confirmed: true` in the tool call to prevent accidental execution.

title: Authentication against the PHP REST API
snippet: No PHP changes are required. The MCP server authenticates using the existing login endpoint: 1. `GET /` — fetches the app home page to obtain a CSRF t
content: No PHP changes are required. The MCP server authenticates using the existing login endpoint: 1. `GET /` — fetches the app home page to obtain a CSRF token 2. `POST /api/auth/login` — submits credentials to receive a JWT 3. All subsequent requests include `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` plus the CSRF token as a query parameter for mutating calls 4. On `401 Unauthorized`, the server re-authenticates automatically The `core` package's `ApiClient` class handles this transparently for all tools.

title: Building for LAMP (production)
snippet: Run from the booking folder: `bash build.sh`, then choose 1 (app files), 2 (database export) or 3 (full mirror: both, plus uploaded images). The step-
content: Run from the booking folder: `bash build.sh`, then choose 1 (app files), 2 (database export) or 3 (full mirror: both, plus uploaded images). The step-by-step deploy is in `wiki/Deployment.md`. **App files (`dist/`)** 1. Rebuilds the CSS (falls back to the committed `css/output.css` if Node fails) 2. rsyncs the app into a fresh `dist/`, excluding everything in `.distignore` 3. Keeps an existing `dist/config/env.php`; otherwise creates it from `config/env-shared.example.php` with a random `APP_KEY` and `JWT_SECRET`. `config/app.php` and `config/database.php` ship unchanged: they read `$_ENV` 4. Creates `storage/`, `logs/` and `uploads/` with their `.htaccess` rules (full mirror: copies the uploaded images too) 5. Refuses to finish if any `.sql` file ended up in `dist/` **Database export (`db-export/`)** 1. Copies `booking_app` into a temporary database: structure via `mysqldump --no-data`, data server-side with `INSERT … SELECT` 2. Cleans the copy: deletes `@test.local` accounts (their rows cascade), empties `audit_logs` and `cache`, deletes `enc:` settings (encrypted with the local `APP_KEY`), sets `notifications_disabled = 1` 3. Converts the copy's text columns to binary and dumps the data with `--hex-blob --replace`. The Galvani MySQL gives the `mysql`/`mysqldump` clients a latin1 session whatever they ask for, so text must never pass through them as text; `--replace` lets the real `notification_templates` rows overwrite the defaults `schema.sql` seeds 4. Writes `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` for every table + `schema.sql` + the data, gzipped, to `db-export/booking-mirror-<date>.sql.gz`, and drops the temporary database `db-export/` is gitignored and excluded from `dist/`: it contains customer data and is imported through phpMyAdmin from your computer, never uploaded.

Pass all params via query string and read from `$_GET`. | | **CSRF token delivery** | Custom headers are dropped on multipart/DELETE requests. Append `_csrf_token` as a query param using `csrfUrl()`. title: Deployment
snippet: This covers deploying WFCS Booking to a **LAMP server** (Apache, PHP, MySQL) with the app at the domain root, using SFTP for files and phpMyAdmin for
content: This covers deploying WFCS Booking to a **LAMP server** (Apache, PHP, MySQL) with the app at the domain root, using SFTP for files and phpMyAdmin for the database. `build.sh` makes two separate things: - **`dist/`** — the app files. You upload the contents of this folder. - **`db-export/`** — a database installer for phpMyAdmin. It contains customer data, so it stays on your computer: you import it from your browser and never upload it to the server. ---

title: Prerequisites
snippet: - PHP 8.1 or newer with `pdo_mysql`, `mbstring`, `curl`, `openssl` and `zip` - MySQL 8 (or MariaDB 10.6+) - Apache with `mod_rewrite`, and `AllowOverr
content: - PHP 8.1 or newer with `pdo_mysql`, `mbstring`, `curl`, `openssl` and `zip` - MySQL 8 (or MariaDB 10.6+) - Apache with `mod_rewrite`, and `AllowOverride All` for the web root (so `.htaccess` works) - phpMyAdmin and an SFTP client (e.g. FileZilla) - Galvani running locally (the database export reads the local database) ---

title: Step 1 — Build
snippet: From the booking folder on your computer: Choose: - **1) App files** — `dist/` only. Use this for code updates. - **2) Database export** — `db-export/
content: From the booking folder on your computer: Choose: - **1) App files** — `dist/` only. Use this for code updates. - **2) Database export** — `db-export/booking-mirror-<date>.sql.gz` only. - **3) Full mirror** — app files, uploaded images and the database export. Use this for the first install. What the build does: 1. Copies the app into `dist/` (everything in `.distignore` is left out: `.env`, docs, tests, dumps, logs, dev scripts). 2. Creates `dist/config/env.php` with a fresh `APP_KEY` and `JWT_SECRET`. On later builds it keeps the `dist/config/env.php` you've already edited. 3. Adds the `uploads/`, `storage/` and `logs/` folders with their `.htaccess` protection, plus the uploaded images for a full mirror. 4. For the database export, makes a temporary copy of the local database and cleans it: - removes the test accounts (`@test.local`), the audit log and the cache - removes the Stripe, JustGiving and SMTP credentials (they're encrypted with your local `APP_KEY`, so they couldn't be read on the server anyway) - leaves email switched off (`notifications_disabled = 1`), so testing on the new server can't email customers The installer takes its table structure from `database/schema.sql` and the data from that cleaned copy. Your local database isn't changed. ---

title: Step 2 — Edit `dist/config/env.php`
snippet: This is the only config file to edit. Fill in: $_ENV['DB_HOST'] = 'localhost'; $_ENV['DB_PORT'] = '3306'; $_ENV['DB_NAME'] = 'your_database'; $_ENV['D
content: This is the only config file to edit. Fill in: $_ENV['DB_HOST'] = 'localhost'; $_ENV['DB_PORT'] = '3306'; $_ENV['DB_NAME'] = 'your_database'; $_ENV['DB_USER'] = 'your_database_user'; $_ENV['DB_PASS'] = 'your_database_password'; `APP_KEY` and `JWT_SECRET` are already filled in with random values. Keep them private, and don't change `APP_KEY` once you've saved credentials in Settings: they're encrypted with it. ---

title: Step 3 — Import the database
snippet: 1. In your hosting control panel, create an empty MySQL database and user (`utf8mb4`, collation `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`). 2. Open phpMyAdmin and select t
content: 1. In your hosting control panel, create an empty MySQL database and user (`utf8mb4`, collation `utf8mb4_unicode_ci`). 2. Open phpMyAdmin and select that database. 3. Choose **Import**, pick the `.sql.gz` file from `db-export/` on your computer, and select **Import**. phpMyAdmin reads `.gz` files directly. 4. Check you see about 40 tables. The installer drops and recreates every table, so importing it again resets the database to the export. Once the import has worked, delete the export from your computer. ---

title: Step 4 — Upload the files
snippet: Upload the **contents** of `dist/` (not the folder itself) to the web root over SFTP. Make sure hidden files are included: `.htaccess` at the root and
content: Upload the **contents** of `dist/` (not the folder itself) to the web root over SFTP. Make sure hidden files are included: `.htaccess` at the root and in `uploads/`, `storage/` and `logs/`. ├── .htaccess ├── index.php ├── app/ ├── config/ │   └── env.php        (your database login and secrets) ├── css/ ├── images/ ├── js/ ├── uploads/ ├── storage/ └── logs/ The app works out its own path, so it also runs from a subfolder if you ever need that. ---

title: Step 5 — Permissions
snippet: PHP must be able to write to `uploads/`, `storage/` and `logs/`. On most hosts `755` folders owned by your account work; if image uploads fail, check
content: PHP must be able to write to `uploads/`, `storage/` and `logs/`. On most hosts `755` folders owned by your account work; if image uploads fail, check the folders belong to the user PHP runs as. ---

title: Step 6 — Check it works
snippet: 1. Visit `https://yourdomain.com/` — you should see the welcome page. 2. Check the protected paths are refused: `https://yourdomain.com/config/env.php
content: 1. Visit `https://yourdomain.com/` — you should see the welcome page. 2. Check the protected paths are refused: `https://yourdomain.com/config/env.php` and `https://yourdomain.com/logs/` should both give **403 Forbidden**. If they don't, `.htaccess` isn't being read: ask your host to enable `AllowOverride All`. 3. Log in as an admin. ---

title: Step 7 — Re-enter credentials
snippet: The export leaves out anything encrypted with your local `APP_KEY`. Re-enter them: - **Settings → Stripe**: publishable key, secret key, webhook signi
content: The export leaves out anything encrypted with your local `APP_KEY`. Re-enter them: - **Settings → Stripe**: publishable key, secret key, webhook signing secret, and the JustGiving details - **Settings → Email**: the SMTP password Then register the Stripe webhook in the Stripe dashboard: - Endpoint URL: `https://yourdomain.com/api/payments/stripe/webhook` - Events: `payment_intent.succeeded`, `payment_intent.payment_failed` Make a test booking with a Stripe test card (`4242 4242 4242 4242`). ---

title: Step 8 — Launch day
snippet: Emails are off. When you're ready, turn them on in **Settings → Email**. ---
content: Emails are off. When you're ready, turn them on in **Settings → Email**. ---

title: Updating after a code change
snippet: 1. Pull the latest code locally and run `bash build.sh`, option **1**. 2. Upload the changed files from `dist/`. Your server's `config/env.php` isn't
content: 1. Pull the latest code locally and run `bash build.sh`, option **1**. 2. Upload the changed files from `dist/`. Your server's `config/env.php` isn't overwritten as long as you don't upload `dist/config/env.php` over it (the build keeps your edited copy in `dist/` anyway). 3. If the release includes a file in `database/migrations/`, run it in phpMyAdmin (**SQL** tab) before or straight after uploading. Don't re-import a mirror export once the site is live: it replaces all live data. ---

title: Commit message style
snippet: This project uses **Conventional Commits** (`type: subject`). **Types:** | Type | When to use | |---|---| | `feat` | New feature or user-visible behav
content: This project uses **Conventional Commits** (`type: subject`). **Types:** | Type | When to use | |---|---| | `feat` | New feature or user-visible behaviour | | `fix` | Bug fix | | `docs` | Documentation only | | `refactor` | Code change with no behaviour change | | `test` | Adding or updating tests | | `chore` | Tooling, config, dependencies | | `style` | CSS/formatting changes only | **Rules:** - Subject line: imperative mood, no trailing period, 72 characters max. - Use the body (after a blank line) for context — what changed and why. - Reference issues with `closes #N` or `refs #N` in the body. **Examples:** Sends an email via Resend when admin promotes a user from the waitlist. The email includes a payment link and expires 24 hours after promotion. closes #18 admin role was incorrectly seeing the Settings tab. Moved the super_admin guard to buildNavForRole() in helpers.php. refs #22 ---

title: PHP-first — no fetch() for server mutations
snippet: Use `<form method="POST">` for all server-side mutations (create, update, delete). Never use `fetch()` or `XMLHttpRequest` to POST data that changes s
content: Use `<form method="POST">` for all server-side mutations (create, update, delete). Never use `fetch()` or `XMLHttpRequest` to POST data that changes server state. `fetch()` is permitted only for: - Reading JSON data to render in the browser (e.g. availability calendar) - DELETE requests via the REST API (where the operation is triggered by a user action in the UI after a confirm dialog)

title: No numeric IDs in URLs
snippet: All customer-facing and instructor-facing URLs use slugs, not numeric database IDs. - Correct: `/activities/monday-evening-football` - Wrong: `/activi
content: All customer-facing and instructor-facing URLs use slugs, not numeric database IDs. - Correct: `/activities/monday-evening-football` - Wrong: `/activities/42` Slug generation is handled automatically by `ActivityRepository` on creation.

title: Popover API for all dialogs
snippet: Every dialog, confirmation, alert, and prompt must use the native **Popover API** (`<div popover="manual">`). **Before writing any dialog, check `book
content: Every dialog, confirmation, alert, and prompt must use the native **Popover API** (`<div popover="manual">`). **Before writing any dialog, check `booking/app/Views/shared/`** — five shared partials are already included in the layout: | File | JS call | |---|---| | `shared/alert-dialog.php` | `showAlert(msg, opts)` | | `shared/confirm-dialog.php` | `showConfirm(msg, opts)` → `Promise<boolean>` | | `shared/prompt-dialog.php` | `showPrompt(msg, opts)` → `Promise<string\|null>` | | `shared/cancel-booking-dialog.php` | cancel booking flow | | `shared/room-booking-dialog.php` | meeting room booking form | Do not: - Use `alert()`, `confirm()`, or `prompt()`. - Use `fixed inset-0 bg-black/50` overlay divs. - Re-include or rewrite shared dialog partials. - Write a new `<div popover="manual">` unless the use case is genuinely not covered by the shared partials.

title: No inline styles
snippet: Never use `style=""` attributes. All styling must be Tailwind utility classes or, where Tailwind is insufficient, a `<style>` block in the view file.
content: Never use `style=""` attributes. All styling must be Tailwind utility classes or, where Tailwind is insufficient, a `<style>` block in the view file. Tailwind classes are mobile-first (`md:`, `lg:` prefixes for larger breakpoints). Design for mobile first.

title: No innerHTML with dynamic data
snippet: Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with dynamic data. This is a hard ban — there are no exceptions. Use DOM methods instead:
content: Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with dynamic data. This is a hard ban — there are no exceptions. Use DOM methods instead: const el = document.createElement('div'); el.textContent = userSuppliedValue; parent.appendChild(el); // To clear and repopulate a container: container.replaceChildren();

title: Repository pattern
snippet: All SQL queries live in `app/Repositories/`. Services contain business logic and call repositories. Controllers orchestrate services. No controller or
content: All SQL queries live in `app/Repositories/`. Services contain business logic and call repositories. Controllers orchestrate services. No controller or service should call `$this->db->query()` directly.

title: DRY — use existing helpers and services
snippet: Before writing new logic, check: - `app/Helpers/` — auth, view rendering, validation, date formatting, CSRF - `app/Services/` — booking, payment, uplo
content: Before writing new logic, check: - `app/Helpers/` — auth, view rendering, validation, date formatting, CSRF - `app/Services/` — booking, payment, upload, notification, session, gift aid - `app/Views/shared/` and `app/Views/partials/atoms/` — reusable UI fragments
